items.stem: Define the term "fraction".
items.answer: A group of hydrocarbons with similar chain lengths and boiling points
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: a group of hydrocarbons with similar chain lengths and boiling points. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain how fractional distillation separates crude oil.
items.answer: Crude oil is vaporised and enters a column that is hot at the bottom and cool at the top; hydrocarbons rise and condense at the level where the temperature is below their boiling point, so fractions with similar boiling points are collected together.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Crude oil is vaporised and enters a column that is hot at the bottom and cool at the top; hydrocarbons rise and condense at the level where the temperature is below their boiling point, so fractions with similar boiling points are collected together. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: "Each fraction is a single pure compound." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Each fraction is a mixture of hydrocarbons with similar chain lengths and boiling points.
items.markingKey: Each fraction is a mixture of hydrocarbons with similar chain lengths and boiling points. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Using Deepwater Horizon oil spill (2010) as an example, explain environmental cost of oil extraction.
items.answer: An explosion on an oil rig in the Gulf of Mexico killed 11 workers and released about 4.9 million barrels of crude oil, harming marine life and coasts. It led to tighter drilling regulations and highlighted the risks of deep-sea oil extraction.
items.markingKey: Context (An explosion on an oil rig in the Gulf of Mexico killed 11 workers and released about 4.9 million barrels of crude oil, harming marine life and coasts.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: It led to tighter drilling regulations and highlighted the risks of deep-sea oil extraction. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to environmental cost of oil extraction.

items.stem: Describe how crude oil is separated into fractions and explain how the properties and uses of the fractions change with chain length.
items.answer: Heat crude oil to ~350 °C to vaporise; vapour enters column (temperature gradient hot at bottom, cool at top); vapours rise, condense at levels below their boiling point; collected on trays. Short chains (C1–C4 refinery gas, petrol C5–C10): low bp, low viscosity, very flammable – fuels for cars, cooking. Medium (kerosene, diesel): jet and lorry fuel. Long (fuel oil, bitumen): high bp, viscous, hard to ignite – ships, roads. Cracking converts surplus long chains into useful short chains.
items.markingKey: Heat crude oil to ~350 °C to vaporise; vapour enters column (temperature gradient hot at bottom, cool at top); vapours rise, condense at levels below their boiling point; collected on trays. Short chains (C1–C4 refinery gas, petrol C5–C10): low bp, low viscosity, very flammable – fuels for cars, cooking. Medium (kerosene, diesel): jet and lorry fuel. Long (fuel oil, bitumen): high bp, viscous, hard to ignite – ships, roads. Cracking converts surplus long chains into useful short chains.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "cracking"?
options: The joining of many alkene monomers by opening their C=C bonds, with no other product
A polymer that softens when heated and can be remoulded
Addition of steam to an alkene using a phosphoric acid catalyst, forming an alcohol
Breaking long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful alkanes and alkenes using heat and a catalyst
items.answer: Breaking long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful alkanes and alkenes using heat and a catalyst
items.markingKey: D. "cracking" is breaking long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful alkanes and alkenes using heat and a catalyst.

items.stem: Explain the difference between a long-chain fraction and a short-chain fraction.
items.answer: Short-chain fractions (gases, petrol) have low boiling points, low viscosity and are very flammable; long-chain fractions (fuel oil, bitumen) have high boiling points, are viscous and hard to ignite.
items.markingKey: Short-chain fractions (gases, petrol) have low boiling points, low viscosity and are very flammable; long-chain fractions (fuel oil, bitumen) have high boiling points, are viscous and hard to ignite. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: An alkane C₁₆H₃₄ is cracked to form one molecule of an alkene with 2 carbon atoms and one alkane. Write the formulae of the two products.
items.answer: C₂H₄ and C₁₄H₃₀
items.markingKey: 1 alkene C₂H₄ (CₙH₂ₙ); 1 alkane C₁₄H₃₀ (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂); carbons and hydrogens balance: 16 C and 34 H.

items.stem: Evaluate the claim: "Crude oil is too valuable to burn and should be kept for making plastics and medicines."
items.answer: Reducing fuel use and keeping oil for chemicals makes sense as renewable energy and electric transport expand.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: finite resource; feedstock for plastics, medicines, lubricants; burning releases CO₂. Arguments against: transport and energy still depend heavily on oil fuels; alternative feedstocks (biomass) are developing. Supported judgement: Reducing fuel use and keeping oil for chemicals makes sense as renewable energy and electric transport expand. items.stem: Explain the difference between a structural formula and a molecular formula.
items.answer: A molecular formula shows the number of each atom (C₂H₆); a structural formula shows how the atoms are bonded (CH₃–CH₃).

items.stem: Name the first four alkanes and alkenes, give their molecular formulae, and explain how the general formulae and functional groups define the two homologous series.
items.answer: Alkanes: methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀ (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, single bonds, saturated). Alkenes: ethene C₂H₄, propene C₃H₆, butene C₄H₈, pentene C₅H₁₀ (CₙH₂ₙ, C=C, unsaturated). Each series differs by CH₂, same functional group → similar reactions; physical properties (bp) increase with chain length.
items.markingKey: Alkanes: methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀ (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, single bonds, saturated). Alkenes: ethene C₂H₄, propene C₃H₆, butene C₄H₈, pentene C₅H₁₀ (CₙH₂ₙ, C=C, unsaturated). Each series differs by CH₂, same functional group → similar reactions; physical properties (bp) increase with chain length.

items.answer: With four carbons, the chain can be straight or branched (methylpropane); three carbons can only be arranged in one way.

items.answer: Complete combustion has plenty of oxygen and forms CO₂ and H₂O; incomplete combustion in limited oxygen forms CO and soot and releases less energy.

items.stem: Briefly describe Brazil’s bioethanol programme (Proálcool, from 1975) and explain what it reveals about renewable fuels from fermentation.
items.answer: Brazil ferments sugar cane to ethanol; most cars run on flex-fuel blends, cutting oil imports and CO₂ emissions. It shows large-scale biofuel use, though it raises land-use and deforestation concerns.

items.stem: Tariq is investigating how the temperature affects the rate of fermentation of glucose by yeast. Formulate a testable hypothesis and justify it using scientific knowledge.
items.answer: If temperature increases up to about 35 °C, then more CO₂ will be produced, because yeast enzymes work faster; above about 45 °C the rate will fall as enzymes are denatured.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: testable prediction in "if … then …" form linking the independent and dependent variables; 1-2 marks: scientific explanation. items.stem: Compare the production of ethanol by fermentation and by hydration of ethene, and evaluate which method a country without oil reserves but with a warm climate should use.
items.answer: Fermentation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂; yeast, 30–35 °C, anaerobic; renewable sugar; batch process, slow, needs distillation; low energy. Hydration: C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH; 300 °C, 60–70 atm, H₃PO₄ catalyst; continuous, fast, pure, high atom economy; needs crude oil. Country: fermentation using sugar cane – renewable, local, no oil imports – but must manage land use.
items.markingKey: Fermentation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂; yeast, 30–35 °C, anaerobic; renewable sugar; batch process, slow, needs distillation; low energy. Hydration: C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH; 300 °C, 60–70 atm, H₃PO₄ catalyst; continuous, fast, pure, high atom economy; needs crude oil. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Distinguish between a short-chain fraction and a long-chain fraction.
items.answer: Short-chain fractions (gases, petrol) have low boiling points, low viscosity and are very flammable; long-chain fractions (fuel oil, bitumen) have high boiling points, are viscous and hard to ignite.
items.markingKey: Short-chain fractions (gases, petrol) have low boiling points, low viscosity and are very flammable; long-chain fractions (fuel oil, bitumen) have high boiling points, are viscous and hard to ignite. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain why hydrogenation is used to make margarine.
items.answer: Adding hydrogen to C=C bonds in vegetable oils raises their melting point, making them solid at room temperature and spreadable.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Adding hydrogen to C=C bonds in vegetable oils raises their melting point, making them solid at room temperature and spreadable. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why fermentation stops when the ethanol concentration reaches about 15%.
items.answer: High ethanol concentrations kill the yeast (denature enzymes and damage membranes), so fermentation stops.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: High ethanol concentrations kill the yeast (denature enzymes and damage membranes), so fermentation stops. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem:
Mohammed measured the mass of a starch-based plastic sample remaining in compost over time (three samples).

Time / weeks | Mass remaining / %: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3

4 | 55 | 53 | 54
6 | 38 | 38 | 40
8 | 28 | 27 | 27
10 | 20 | 20 | 20

Describe the trend shown by the results and explain it using scientific knowledge.
items.answer: The percentage of mass remaining decreases with time, quickly at first and then more slowly. Microorganisms in compost secrete enzymes that break down the starch-based polymer; as the material is used up, there is less left to digest each week.
items.markingKey: 1 trend: The percentage of mass remaining decreases with time, quickly at first and then more slowly.; 1 use of data (quote means/values); 1-2 explanation: Microorganisms in compost secrete enzymes that break down the starch-based polymer; as the material is used up, there is less left to digest each week.

items.stem: Felix is investigating how the number of carbon atoms in an alkane affects the energy released per gram when it burns. Formulate a testable hypothesis and justify it using scientific knowledge.
items.answer: If the alkane has more carbon atoms, then the energy released per gram will be similar (about 45 kJ/g), but the energy per mole will increase, because each extra CH₂ adds similar bonds to be broken and formed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: testable prediction in "if … then …" form linking the independent and dependent variables; 1-2 marks: scientific explanation. Model: If the alkane has more carbon atoms, then the energy released per gram will be similar (about 45 kJ/g), but the energy per mole will increase, because each extra CH₂ adds similar bonds to be broken and formed.

items.stem: In an investigation into how the chain length of an alkane affects its viscosity, explain why this control must be applied in the same way in every trial: releasing from rest at the surface.
items.answer: pushing changes the speed
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a change in this variable (releasing from rest at the surface) would also affect the dependent variable; 1 mark for the specific reason: pushing changes the speed. Then only the independent variable is responsible for any change (validity).

items.stem: Outline one way in which Leaded petrol phase-out (completed 2021) shows chemistry of fuels and health.
items.answer: Tetraethyl lead was added to petrol to stop engine knocking; it caused lead poisoning and lowered children’s IQ; Algeria was the last country to stop selling it in 2021. A UN campaign estimated the phase-out prevents over a million premature deaths a year.
items.markingKey: Context (Tetraethyl lead was added to petrol to stop engine knocking; it caused lead poisoning and lowered children’s IQ; Algeria was the last country to stop selling it in 2021.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: A UN campaign estimated the phase-out prevents over a million premature deaths a year. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to chemistry of fuels and health.

items.answer: How does temperature of the water bath affect volume of CO₂ collected in a gas syringe in 20 minutes?
items.markingKey: 1 mark: names the independent variable (temperature of the water bath (15, 25, 35, 45, 55 °C)); 1 mark: names the measurable dependent variable (volume of CO₂ collected in a gas syringe in 20 minutes) in a question form.

items.stem: Design a safe and valid method to investigate how the chain length of an alkane affects its viscosity. In your answer include the variables, the equipment, the range and number of values of the independent variable, the number of repeats, safety and how the data will be recorded and processed.
items.answer: Fill identical measuring cylinders to the same height with each hydrocarbon in a fume cupboard; mark two lines 20 cm apart; release the ball at the surface; time it between the lines; repeat five times; calculate means; plot fall time against carbon number.
items.markingKey: MYP criterion B: 1 independent variable with at least 5 values in a sensible range; 1 dependent variable and how it is measured; 1 at least two controls and how they are controlled; 1 logical step-by-step procedure with equipment; 1 at least 3 repeats and calculation of a mean; 1 relevant safety point (hydrocarbons are flammable and harmful – use a fume cupboard, no flames, eye protection). Model: Fill identical measuring cylinders to the same height with each hydrocarbon in a fume cupboard; mark two lines 20 cm apart; release the ball at the surface; time it between the lines; repeat five times; calculate means; plot fall time against carbon number.

items.stem: Write balanced equations for the complete combustion of propane and its incomplete combustion forming carbon monoxide, and evaluate the dangers of using a gas heater in a poorly ventilated room.
items.answer: Complete: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. Incomplete (CO): 2C₃H₈ + 7O₂ → 6CO + 8H₂O. In poor ventilation oxygen runs low → incomplete combustion → toxic CO (colourless, odourless, binds haemoglobin, can kill) and soot; also less energy released. Need ventilation, servicing and CO alarms.
items.markingKey: Complete: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. Incomplete (CO): 2C₃H₈ + 7O₂ → 6CO + 8H₂O. In poor ventilation oxygen runs low → incomplete combustion → toxic CO (colourless, odourless, binds haemoglobin, can kill) and soot; also less energy released. Need ventilation, servicing and CO alarms.

items.stem: "Bioethanol is a sustainable replacement for petrol." To what extent is this view justified?
items.answer: Bioethanol from waste or non-food crops can be sustainable; from food crops on cleared land it may not be.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: renewable; CO₂ absorbed by crops partly balances CO₂ from burning; reduces dependence on oil imports. Arguments against: uses farmland that could grow food; fertiliser, processing and transport emissions; possible deforestation. Supported judgement: Bioethanol from waste or non-food crops can be sustainable; from food crops on cleared land it may not be. Markbands (8 marks): MYP criterion D (0-8, scaled): 7-8 explains thoroughly how the science is applied to address the issue, discusses and evaluates the implications (moral, ethical, social, economic, political, cultural or environmental), and documents sources consistently; 5-6 explains and discusses; 3-4 outlines; 1-2 states.

items.stem: "Single-use plastics should be banned worldwide." To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: Bans on avoidable single-use items are justified, with exemptions for essential uses and investment in alternatives.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: reduces ocean pollution and litter; encourages reusable alternatives. Arguments against: some single-use plastics are essential (medical equipment, food hygiene); alternatives (paper, glass) may have higher carbon footprints. Supported judgement: Bans on avoidable single-use items are justified, with exemptions for essential uses and investment in alternatives. Markbands (15 marks): MYP criterion D (0-8, scaled): 7-8 explains thoroughly how the science is applied to address the issue, discusses and evaluates the implications (moral, ethical, social, economic, political, cultural or environmental), and documents sources consistently; 5-6 explains and discusses; 3-4 outlines; 1-2 states.

items.answer: functional group

items.answer: viscosity
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of viscosity.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "hydration".
items.answer: Addition of steam to an alkene using a phosphoric acid catalyst, forming an alcohol

items.answer: ethyl butanoate; water; concentrated sulfuric acid

items.answer: ethene

items.stem: Briefly explain why members of a homologous series have similar chemical reactions.
items.answer: They have the same functional group, which is where reactions happen.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: They have the same functional group, which is where reactions happen. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why short-chain hydrocarbons make better fuels than long-chain ones.
items.answer: They ignite more easily (more flammable), are less viscous, flow easily and burn more cleanly with a less smoky flame.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: They ignite more easily (more flammable), are less viscous, flow easily and burn more cleanly with a less smoky flame. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between a substitution reaction and an addition reaction.
items.answer: In substitution an atom is replaced by another (alkanes with halogens in UV light); in addition atoms add across a double bond and no atoms are lost (alkenes).
items.markingKey: In substitution an atom is replaced by another (alkanes with halogens in UV light); in addition atoms add across a double bond and no atoms are lost (alkenes). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: "All alcohols are safe to drink in small amounts." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Methanol is highly toxic and can cause blindness and death; only ethanol is in drinks and it is also harmful in excess.
items.markingKey: Methanol is highly toxic and can cause blindness and death; only ethanol is in drinks and it is also harmful in excess. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A student claims: "All plastics can be recycled together." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Different polymers must be sorted by type (resin codes), as mixed plastics produce weak, low-quality material.
items.markingKey: Different polymers must be sorted by type (resin codes), as mixed plastics produce weak, low-quality material. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Give one argument for and one argument against this view: "Crude oil is too valuable to burn and should be kept for making plastics and medicines."
items.answer: Reducing fuel use and keeping oil for chemicals makes sense as renewable energy and electric transport expand.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: finite resource; feedstock for plastics, medicines, lubricants; burning releases CO₂. items.stem: Evaluate the claim: "Petrol and diesel cars should be banned in cities."
items.answer: Gradual bans with support and clean electricity improve health and climate.

items.stem: Design a safe and valid method to investigate how the temperature affects the rate of fermentation of glucose by yeast. In your answer include the variables, the equipment, the range and number of values of the independent variable, the number of repeats, safety and how the data will be recorded and processed.
items.answer: Mix 2 g yeast with 50 cm³ of 10% glucose in a flask; cover with oil; connect to a gas syringe; place in a water bath for 10 min; record the gas volume over 20 min; repeat at each temperature three times; plot volume against temperature.
items.markingKey: MYP criterion B: 1 independent variable with at least 5 values in a sensible range; 1 dependent variable and how it is measured; 1 at least two controls and how they are controlled; 1 logical step-by-step procedure with equipment; 1 at least 3 repeats and calculation of a mean; 1 relevant safety point (hot water baths – take care; wash hands; flasks under pressure could pop bungs – use a gas syringe). Model: Mix 2 g yeast with 50 cm³ of 10% glucose in a flask; cover with oil; connect to a gas syringe; place in a water bath for 10 min; record the gas volume over 20 min; repeat at each temperature three times; plot volume against temperature.
